Resolve decision contract: post-Pluck outcome analysis.\n//!\n//! This module implements a structured decision system that runs after a Pluck\n//! operation completes. The resolver analyzes the agent's work and determines\n//! the appropriate next action, with strict validation and fail-safe defaults.\n//!\n//! ## Decision Flow\n//!\n//! 1. Agent completes Pluck (exit code 0 or non-zero)\n//! 2. Resolver receives agent output and context\n//! 3. Structured prompt is built from the resolve template\n//! 4. Agent must respond with valid JSON matching the schema\n//! 5. Parser validates the response exhaustively\n//! 6. Invalid/incomplete/unknown decisions fall back to safe defaults\n//!\n//! ## Decision Types\n//!\n//! - **Complete**: Task succeeded, bead should be closed\n//! - **Retry**: Temporary failure, release for immediate retry\n//! - **Blocked**: External dependency, cannot proceed without human input\n//! - **Split**: Task decomposes into multiple independent subtasks\n//!\n//! ## Safety Guarantees\n//!\n//! - Resolver NEVER implements changes or mutates beads\n//! - Invalid JSON → fallback to Retry (safe default)\n//! - Unknown decision type → fallback to Retry\n//! - Missing required fields → fallback to Retry\n//! - Timeout → fallback to Retry\n//!\n//! Depends on: `types`, `prompt`, `config`, `telemetry`.\n\nuse std::fmt;\nuse std::time::Duration;\n\nuse anyhow::{bail, Context, Result};\nuse chrono::{DateTime, Utc};\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\n\nuse crate::prompt::PromptBuilder;\nuse crate::telemetry::Telemetry;\nuse crate::types::Bead;\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ResolveDecision enum\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The four exhaustive resolve decision types.\n///\n/// Every possible post-Pluck outcome maps to exactly one of these decisions.\n/// No wildcards in matching — all variants must be explicitly handled.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum ResolveDecision {\n    /// Task completed successfully — close the bead.\n    Complete {\n        /// Evidence that the task succeeded (git commits, tests passed, etc.)\n        evidence: String,\n        /// Human-readable summary of what was accomplished.\n        summary: String,\n    },\n\n    /// Temporary failure — release bead for immediate retry.\n    Retry {\n        /// Why the attempt failed (error message, diagnostic info).\n        reason: String,\n        /// Suggested retry strategy (same approach, different timeout, etc.).\n        strategy: RetryStrategy,\n    },\n\n    /// Blocked by external dependency — cannot proceed without human input.\n    Blocked {\n        /// What external resource is blocking progress (API, human decision, etc).\n        blocker: String,\n        /// What action is needed from a human (approve plan, provide credentials, etc).\n        required_action: String,\n        /// How critical this block is to project progress.\n        severity: BlockSeverity,\n    },\n\n    /// Task decomposes into multiple independent subtasks.\n    Split {\n        /// Proposed child beads (independent, sequentially completable).\n        children: Vec<ProposedChild>,\n        /// Rationale for why this decomposition is appropriate.\n        rationale: String,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl ResolveDecision {\n    /// Returns the decision type as a string for telemetry.\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            ResolveDecision::Complete { .. } => \"complete\",\n            ResolveDecision::Retry { .. } => \"retry\",\n            ResolveDecision::Blocked { .. } => \"blocked\",\n            ResolveDecision::Split { .. } => \"split\",\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Validate the decision has all required fields populated.\n    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        match self {\n            ResolveDecision::Complete { evidence, summary } => {\n                if evidence.trim().is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Complete decision missing evidence\");\n                }\n                if summary.trim().is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Complete decision missing summary\");\n                }\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            ResolveDecision::Retry { reason, strategy } => {\n                if reason.trim().is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Retry decision missing reason\");\n                }\n                strategy.validate()?;\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            ResolveDecision::Blocked {\n                blocker,\n                required_action,\n                severity,\n            } => {\n                if blocker.trim().is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Blocked decision missing blocker\");\n                }\n                if required_action.trim().is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Blocked decision missing required_action\");\n                }\n                severity.validate()?;\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            ResolveDecision::Split {\n                children,\n                rationale,\n            } => {\n                if children.is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Split decision must have at least one child\");\n                }\n                if children.len() > 10 {\n                    bail!(\"Split decision cannot have more than 10 children\");\n                }\n                for (idx, child) in children.iter().enumerate() {\n                    child.validate(idx)?;\n                }\n                if rationale.trim().is_empty() {\n                    bail!(\"Split decision missing rationale\");\n                }\n                Ok(())\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for ResolveDecision {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            ResolveDecision::Complete { summary, .. } => {\n                write!(f, \"Complete: {}\", summary)\n            }\n            ResolveDecision::Retry { reason, .. } => {\n                write!(f, \"Retry: {}\", reason)\n            }\n            ResolveDecision::Blocked {\n                blocker,\n                required_action,\n                ..\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"Blocked on {}: {}\", blocker, required_action)\n            }\n            ResolveDecision::Split { children, .. } => {\n                write!(f, \"Split into {} child tasks\", children.len())\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// RetryStrategy\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Strategy for retrying a failed attempt.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum RetryStrategy {\n    /// Same approach should work (transient failure, rate limit, etc).\n    Same,\n    /// Increase timeout for next attempt.\n    IncreaseTimeout,\n    /// Different approach needed (implementation incorrect, API changed, etc).\n    DifferentApproach,\n    /// Resource unavailable (service down, dependency missing, etc).\n    Backoff,\n}\n\nimpl RetryStrategy {\n    fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        // All variants are valid by construction\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            RetryStrategy::Same => \"same\",\n            RetryStrategy::IncreaseTimeout => \"increase_timeout\",\n            RetryStrategy::DifferentApproach => \"different_approach\",\n            RetryStrategy::Backoff => \"backoff\",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// BlockSeverity\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// How critical a blocker is to project progress.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum BlockSeverity {\n    /// Cosmetic issue, nice-to-have enhancement, or low-priority cleanup.\n    Low,\n    /// Feature complete but blocked on polish, tests, or documentation.\n    Medium,\n    /// Critical blocker preventing core functionality or release.\n    High,\n}\n\nimpl BlockSeverity {\n    fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        // All variants are valid by construction\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            BlockSeverity::Low => \"low\",\n            BlockSeverity::Medium => \"medium\",\n            BlockSeverity::High => \"high\",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ProposedChild\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A proposed child bead from a Split decision.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct ProposedChild {\n    /// Short title for the child task.\n    pub title: String,\n    /// Detailed description and acceptance criteria.\n    pub body: String,\n    /// Recommended priority (1-4, lower is higher priority).\n    pub priority: u8,\n}\n\nimpl ProposedChild {\n    fn validate(&self, idx: usize) -> Result<()> {\n        if self.title.trim().is_empty() {\n            bail!(\"Child {} has empty title\", idx);\n        }\n        if self.body.trim().is_empty() {\n            bail!(\"Child {} ({}) has empty body\", idx, self.title);\n        }\n        if !(1..=4).contains(&self.priority) {\n            bail!(\n                \"Child {} ({}) has invalid priority {}, must be 1-4\",\n                idx,\n                self.title,\n                self.priority\n            );\n        }\n        if self.title.len() > 200 {\n            bail!(\n                \"Child {} title too long ({} chars, max 200)\",\n                idx,\n                self.title.len()\n            );\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ResolveResponse\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The structured response schema for the resolve prompt.\n///\n/// Agents must respond with exactly this structure. All fields are required\n/// for the decision to be valid.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct ResolveResponse {\n    /// The decision type (one of: complete, retry, blocked, split).\n    pub decision: ResolveDecision,\n}\n\nimpl ResolveResponse {\n    /// Parse and validate a JSON response string.\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if:\n    /// - JSON is malformed\n    /// - Structure doesn't match ResolveResponse\n    /// - Decision is invalid per validate()\n    pub fn parse_and_validate(json: &str) -> Result<Self> {\n        // First, try to parse as JSON\n        let response: Self = serde_json::from_str(json)\n            .with_context(|| \"failed to parse resolve response as JSON\")?;\n\n        // Then validate the decision structure\n        response\n            .decision\n            .validate()\n            .with_context(|| \"parsed decision failed validation\")?;\n\n        Ok(response)\n    }\n\n    /// Check if the response JSON is valid without fully parsing.\n    ///\n    /// This is a cheap pre-check before attempting full parsing.\n    pub fn looks_valid(json: &str) -> bool {\n        // Quick heuristic checks\n        let json = json.trim();\n\n        // Must be non-empty and start with {\n        if json.is_empty() || !json.starts_with('{') {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // Must contain a decision field\n        if !json.contains(\"\\\"decision\\\"\") {\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // Must contain one of the decision type markers\n        json.contains(\"\\\"complete\\\"\")\n            || json.contains(\"\\\"retry\\\"\")\n            || json.contains(\"\\\"blocked\\\"\")\n            || json.contains(\"\\\"split\\\"\")\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ResolveContext\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Context passed to the resolver for decision-making.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ResolveContext<'a> {\n    /// The bead being resolved.\n    pub bead: &'a Bead,\n    /// Agent exit code from Pluck.\n    pub exit_code: i32,\n    /// Agent stdout output.\n    pub stdout: String,\n    /// Agent stderr output.\n    pub stderr: String,\n    /// Duration of the Pluck operation.\n    pub duration: Duration,\n    /// Timestamp when Pluck started.\n    pub started_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n    /// Whether the operation was interrupted (SIGINT/SIGTERM).\n    pub was_interrupted: bool,\n}\n\nimpl<'a> ResolveContext<'a> {\n    /// Create a new resolve context.\n    pub fn new(\n        bead: &'a Bead,\n        exit_code: i32,\n        stdout: String,\n        stderr: String,\n        duration: Duration,\n        started_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n        was_interrupted: bool,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            bead,\n            exit_code,\n            stdout,\n            stderr,\n            duration,\n            started_at,\n            was_interrupted,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Format the duration for display in the prompt.\n    pub fn formatted_duration(&self) -> String {\n        let secs = self.duration.as_secs();\n        if secs >= 3600 {\n            format!(\"{}h {}m\", secs / 3600, (secs % 3600) / 60)\n        } else if secs >= 60 {\n            format!(\"{}m {}s\", secs / 60, secs % 60)\n        } else {\n            format!(\"{}s\", secs)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get a truncated version of stdout for the prompt (max 2000 chars).\n    pub fn truncated_stdout(&self) -> String {\n        self.stdout.chars().take(2000).collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Get a truncated version of stderr for the prompt (max 2000 chars).\n    pub fn truncated_stderr(&self) -> String {\n        self.stderr.chars().take(2000).collect()\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// VerificationError\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Error type for binary identity verification failures.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum VerificationError {\n    /// Binary identity verification failed.\n    VerificationFailed(String),\n    /// Verification not supported for this binary type.\n    NotSupported(String),\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for VerificationError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            VerificationError::VerificationFailed(msg) => {\n                write!(f, \"Verification failed: {}\", msg)\n            }\n            VerificationError::NotSupported(msg) => {\n                write!(f, \"Verification not supported: {}\", msg)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for VerificationError {}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Resolver\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The resolver analyzes Pluck outcomes and determines next actions.\npub struct Resolver {\n    /// Timeout for resolve agent calls (default 120s).\n    timeout: Duration,\n    /// Prompt builder for constructing the resolve prompt.\n    prompt_builder: PromptBuilder,\n    /// Telemetry client for emitting events.\n    telemetry: Option<Telemetry>,\n}\n\nimpl Resolver {\n    /// Create a new resolver with default timeout.\n    pub fn new(prompt_builder: PromptBuilder) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            timeout: Duration::from_secs(120),\n            prompt_builder,\n            telemetry: None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Set the timeout for resolve agent calls.\n    pub fn with_timeout(mut self, timeout: Duration) -> Self {\n        self.timeout = timeout;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Set the telemetry client for event emission.\n    pub fn with_telemetry(mut self, telemetry: Telemetry) -> Self {\n        self.telemetry = Some(telemetry);\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Resolve a Pluck outcome into a structured decision.\n    ///\n    /// This method:\n    /// 1. Builds the resolve prompt with context\n    /// 2. Invokes an agent to analyze and decide\n    /// 3. Parses and validates the response\n    /// 4. Verifies binary identity after successful resolution\n    /// 5. Returns the decision or a safe fallback\n    ///\n    /// # Safety\n    ///\n    /// Any failure (timeout, invalid JSON, parse error, validation error, verification failure)\n    /// returns a safe fallback decision (Retry with generic reason) rather\n    /// than propagating the error. This ensures the worker can always continue.\n    pub async fn resolve(&self, context: &ResolveContext<'_>) -> ResolveDecision {\n        tracing::info!(\n            bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n            exit_code = context.exit_code,\n            \"resolver: starting analysis\"\n        );\n\n        // Build the resolve prompt\n        let prompt = match self.build_prompt(context) {\n            Ok(p) => p,\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"resolver: failed to build prompt, using fallback\"\n                );\n                return self.fallback_decision(\"prompt_build_failed\");\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Invoke the resolve agent with timeout\n        let response_text = match self.invoke_resolve_agent(&prompt).await {\n            Ok(text) => text,\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"resolver: agent invocation failed, using fallback\"\n                );\n                return self.fallback_decision(\"agent_invocation_failed\");\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Parse and validate the response\n        let decision = match self.parse_and_validate_response(&response_text) {\n            Ok(decision) => decision,\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    response = %response_text,\n                    \"resolver: response parsing/validation failed, using fallback\"\n                );\n                return self.fallback_decision(\"response_validation_failed\");\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Verify binary identity after successful resolution\n        if let Err(e) = self.verify_binary_identity(&decision) {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n                error = %e,\n                \"resolver: binary identity verification failed, using fallback\"\n            );\n            return ResolveDecision::Retry {\n                reason: format!(\"Binary identity verification failed: {}\", e),\n                strategy: RetryStrategy::DifferentApproach,\n            };\n        }\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            bead_id = %context.bead.id,\n            decision = %decision.as_str(),\n            \"resolver: decision successfully determined\"\n        );\n\n        decision\n    }\n\n    /// Invoke the resolve agent with the given prompt.\n    ///\n    /// Returns the agent's raw text response or an error.\n    async fn invoke_resolve_agent(&self, prompt: &str) -> Result<String> {\n        use std::process::Stdio;\n        use tokio::process::Command as AsyncCommand;\n\n        tracing::debug!(\n            prompt_length = prompt.len(),\n            \"resolver: invoking resolve agent\"\n        );\n\n        // Use claude CLI for resolve analysis\n        let output = tokio::time::timeout(self.timeout, async {\n            let child = AsyncCommand::new(\"claude\")\n                .arg(\"--message\")\n                .arg(prompt)\n                .stdout(Stdio::piped())\n                .stderr(Stdio::piped())\n                .spawn()\n                .context(\"failed to spawn resolve agent\")?;\n\n            child\n                .wait_with_output()\n                .await\n                .context(\"failed to wait for resolve agent\")\n        })\n        .await\n        .context(\"resolve agent invocation timed out\")??;\n\n        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).to_string();\n        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).to_string();\n\n        if !output.status.success() {\n            anyhow::bail!(\n                \"resolve agent exited with {}: {}\",\n                output.status,\n                stderr.trim()\n            );\n        }\n\n        tracing::debug!(\n            response_length = stdout.len(),\n            \"resolver: agent response received\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(stdout)\n    }\n\n    /// Parse and validate the agent's response text.\n    ///\n    /// Returns the validated decision or an error.\n    fn parse_and_validate_response(&self, response_text: &str) -> Result<ResolveDecision> {\n        // Strip markdown code fencing if present\n        let cleaned = response_text\n            .trim()\n            .trim_start_matches(\"```json\")\n            .trim_end_matches(\"```\")\n            .trim();\n\n        // Try to parse as ResolveResponse\n        let response = ResolveResponse::parse_and_validate(cleaned)?;\n\n        // Return the decision (already validated by parse_and_validate)\n        Ok(response.decision)\n    }\n\n    /// Build the resolve prompt from context.\n    fn build_prompt(&self, context: &ResolveContext<'_>) -> Result<String> {\n        let worker_id = \"resolver\"; // Resolver doesn't have a worker ID\n\n        let exit_status = if context.exit_code == 0 {\n            \"success\"\n        } else {\n            \"failure\"\n        };\n        let was_interrupted = if context.was_interrupted {\n            \"true\"\n        } else {\n            \"false\"\n        };\n\n        // Build the prompt with resolve-specific variables using the dedicated method\n        let built = self.prompt_builder.build_resolve(\n            context.bead,\n            &context.bead.workspace,\n            worker_id,\n            context.exit_code,\n            &context.formatted_duration(),\n            &context.truncated_stdout(),\n            &context.truncated_stderr(),\n            exit_status,\n            was_interrupted,\n        )?;\n\n        Ok(built.content)\n    }\n\n    /// Return a safe fallback decision.\n    ///\n    /// This is used when:\n    /// - Prompt building fails\n    /// - Agent invocation times out\n    /// - JSON parsing fails\n    /// - Decision validation fails\n    fn fallback_decision(&self, reason: &str) -> ResolveDecision {\n        ResolveDecision::Retry {\n            reason: format!(\n                \"Resolver error: {}. Safe fallback: retry with same approach.\",\n                reason\n            ),\n            strategy: RetryStrategy::Same,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Verify binary identity after successful resolution.\n    ///\n    /// This is a placeholder hook for binary identity verification.\n    /// Currently returns Ok(()) as a stub implementation.\n    ///\n    /// # Future Implementation\n    ///\n    /// This method should:\n    /// - Verify the binary matches expected checksums\n    /// - Validate binary signatures\n    /// - Check binary integrity\n    /// - Ensure the binary is from a trusted source\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    ///\n    /// - `Ok(())` - Verification passed\n    /// - `Err(VerificationError)` - Verification failed\n    fn verify_binary_identity(&self, _decision: &ResolveDecision) -> Result<(), VerificationError> {\n        // Stub implementation - always passes for now\n        // TODO: Implement actual verification logic\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// /// Select the variant version for a given template and worker.\n1131\t    ///\n1132\t    /// Returns `(template_version, variant_content)`:\n1133\t    /// - `template_version`: e.g. `\"pluck-default\"` or `\"pluck-v2\"`\n1134\t    /// - `variant_content`: `Some(String)` if a variant file was loaded, `None` for the default\n1135\t    ///\n1136\t    /// Assignment is deterministic: `worker_bucket(worker_id)` in `[0, 99]` is compared\n1137\t    /// against cumulative variant weights.  Same `worker_id` always produces the same result.\n1138\t    fn select_variant(\n1139\t        &self,\n1140\t        worker_id: &str,\n1141\t        template_name: &str,\n1142\t        workspace: &Path,\n1143\t    ) -> (String, Option<String>) {\n1144\t        let Some(variants) = self.variants.get(template_name) else {\n1145\t            return (format!(\"{template_name}-default\"), None);\n1146\t        };\n1147\t\n1148\t        if variants.is_empty() {\n1149\t            return (format!(\"{template_name}-default\"), None);\n1150\t        }\n1151\t\n1152\t        let bucket = worker_bucket(worker_id);\n1153\t        let mut cumulative: u32 = 0;\n1154\t\n1155\t        for variant in variants {\n1156\t            cumulative += u32::from(variant.weight);\n1157\t            if u32::from(bucket) < cumulative {\n1158\t                let abs_path = workspace.join(&variant.content_file);\n1159\t                match std::fs::read_to_string(&abs_path) {\n1160\t                    Ok(content) => {\n1161\t                        return (format!(\"{template_name}-{}\", variant.name), Some(content));\n1162\t                    }\n1163\t                    Err(_) => {\n1164\t                        // Content file missing — fall back to the built-in default.\n1165\t                        return (format!(\"{template_name}-default\"), None);\n1166\t                    }\n1167\t                }\n1168\t            }\n1169\t        }\n1170\t\n1171\t        // Cumulative weights < 100: worker falls outside all variant ranges.\n1172\t        (format!(\"{template_name}-default\"), None)\n1173\t    }\n1174\t}\n1175\t\n1176\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n1177\t// Helpers\n1178\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n1179\t\n1180\t/// Compute the worker's variant bucket: `hash(worker_id) % 100` in `[0, 99]`.\n1181\t///\n1182\t/// Uses the first 8 bytes of the SHA-256 digest of `worker_id` as a `u64`,\n1183\t/// then takes modulo 100.  The result is deterministic and stable.\n1184\tfn worker_bucket(worker_id: &str) -> u8 {\n1185\t    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();\n1186\t    hasher.update(worker_id.as_bytes());\n1187\t    let SHA-256 hex digest of a string.\n1193\tfn hex_sha256(s: &str) -> String {\n1194\t    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();\n1195\t    hasher.update(s.as_bytes());\n1196\t    let result = hasher.finalize();\n1197\t    // Format as lowercase hex\n1198\t    result.iter().fold(String::with_capacity(64), |mut acc, b| {\n1199\t        use std::fmt::Write;\n1200\t        let _ = write!(acc, \"{b:02x}\");\n1201\t        acc\n1202\t    })\n1203\t}\n1204\t\n1205\t/// Format bead comments for inclusion in the prompt.\n1206\t///\n1207\t/// Comments are rendered with newest first (reverse chronological order).\n1208\t/// Total output is capped at `MAX_COMMENTS_BYTES`; if exceeded, the oldest\n1209\t/// comments are truncated and a note is appended.\n1210\t///\n1211\t/// The format includes:\n1212\t/// - Author and timestamp for each comment\n1213\t/// - Clear delimiters between comments\n1214\t/// - Explicit instruction that later comments supersede earlier ones\n1215\tfn format_comments(comments: &[crate::types::Comment]) -> String {\n1216\t    const MAX_COMMENTS_BYTES: usize = 2000;\n1217\t\n1218\t    if comments.is_empty() {\n1219\t        return String::new();\n1220\t    }\n1221\t\n1222\t    let mut output = String::from(\"## Comments (newest first)\\n\\n\");\n1223\t    output.push_str(\n1224\t        \"IMPORTANT: Later comments supersede the description above. \\\n1225\t        If a comment conflicts with the description, follow the comment.\\n\\n\",\n1226\t    );\n1227\t\n1228\t    // Sort comments by created_at descending (newest first) and accumulate\n1229\t    let mut sorted_comments: Vec<_> = comments.iter().collect();\n1230\t    sorted_comments.sort_by_key(|comment| std::cmp::Reverse(comment.created_at));\n1231\t\n1232\t    let mut total_bytes = output.len();\n1233\t    let mut truncated = false;\n1234\t    let mut displayed_count = 0;\n1235\t\n1236\t    for (idx, comment) in sorted_comments.iter().enumerate() {\n1237\t        let comment_text = format!(\n1238\t            \"### Comment {} (by {}, {})\\n{}\\n\\n\",\n1239\t            idx + 1,\n1240\t            comment.author,\n1241\t            comment.created_at.format(\"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S UTC\"),\n1242\t            comment.text\n1243\t        );\n1244\t\n1245\t        // Check if adding this comment would exceed the cap\n1246\t        if      total_bytes += comment_text.len();\n1253\t        displayed_count += 1;\n1254\t    }\n1255\t\n1256\t    if truncated {\n1257\t        let omitted = sorted_comments.len() - omitted\n1261\t        );\n1262\t        output.push_str(&note);\n1263\t    }\n1264\t\n1265\t    output\n1266\t}\n1267\t\n1268\t/// Extract all `{variable}` references from a template `\"{bead_id}\"`).\n1272\tfn extract_template_vars(template: &str) -> Vec<String> {\n1273\t    let mut vars = Vec::new();\n1274\t    let chars: Vec<char> = template.chars().collect();\n1275\t    let {\n1302\t            i += 1;\n1303\t        }\n1304\t    }\n1305\t\n1306\t    vars\n1307\t}\n1308\t\n1309\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n1310\t// Depends on: `types`, `config`.\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse std::path::Path;\n\nuse anyhow::{bail, Context, Result};\nuse sha2::{Digest, Sha256};\n\nuse crate::config::{PromptConfig, VariantConfig};\nuse crate::learning::{GlobalLearningsFile, LearningsFile};\nuse crate::skill::SkillLibrary;\nuse crate::types::Bead;\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Default templates\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Built-in pluck template used when no override is configured.\nconst DEFAULT_PLUCK_TEMPLATE: &str = \"\\\n## Task\n\n{bead_title}\n\n## Description\n\n{bead_body}\n\n{bead_comments}\n\n## Workspace\n\n{workspace_path}\n\n## Context Files\n\n{context_file_contents}\n\n## Instructions\n\n{workspace_instructions}\n\nComplete the task described above. When finished:\n- **If you changed files, commit and push them.** `git commit`, then `git push`. Real\n  changes are source, tests, config, or documentation the task actually asked for.\n- **If the task needed no file changes, do NOT manufacture a commit.** Verification-only\n  work, work that turned out to be already done, and work you found blocked are all\n  legitimate outcomes with nothing to commit. Record the finding on the bead instead:\n\n`{bead_cli} update {bead_id} --notes \\\"what you checked and what you found\\\"`\n\n  Never create `notes/{bead_id}.md`, a summary, a report, or a status file to satisfy a\n  commit requirement. Status belongs on the bead, not in git history. A commit whose only\n  changes are under `notes/` or `.beads/` does not count as shipped work and will be\n  rejected.\n- Close the bead:\n\n`{bead_cli} close {bead_id} --reason \\\"...\\\"`\n\nIf you cannot complete the task:\n- Do NOT close the bead\n- The bead will be automatically released for retry\n\nBead ID: {bead_id}\";\n\n/// Built-in mitosis analysis template.\n///\n/// The agent receives the bead context and must output JSON describing whether\n/// the bead contains multiple independent tasks and, if so, proposed child beads.\nconst DEFAULT_MITOSIS_TEMPLATE: &str = \"\\\n## Mitosis Analysis\n\nAnalyze the following bead and determine if it describes MULTIPLE INDEPENDENT TASKS.\n\n### Bead\n\n**Title:** {bead_title}\n\n**Description:**\n{bead_body}\n\n**Bead ID:** {bead_id}\n\n### Existing Children\n\n{existing_children}\n\n### Instructions\n\nYou must output ONLY a JSON object (no markdown fencing, no explanation).\n\nIf the bead describes multiple independent tasks that can be worked on separately:\n{{\\\"splittable\\\": true, \\\"children\\\": [{{\\\"title\\\": \\\"Short task title\\\", \\\"body\\\": \\\"Task description and acceptance criteria\\\"}}, ...]}}\n\nIf the bead describes a single task (even if complex or long):\n{{\\\"splittable\\\": false}}\n\n### Rules for splitting\n\n- Split ONLY if the bead asks for MORE THAN ONE independent unit of work\n- Each child must be independently completable and closable\n- Valid split: \\\"add endpoint AND write migration AND update tests\\\" (three deliverables)\n- Invalid split: bead is long, bead failed, bead has many acceptance criteria for one task\n- Preserve the original acceptance criteria by distributing them to the appropriate child\n- Each child title should be concise and start with a verb\n- Do not propose children that duplicate any existing children listed above\";\n\n/// Built-in timeout-specific mitosis analysis template.\n///\n/// This template is used when a bead times out after productive work.\n/// The agent must analyze what was completed and decompose remaining work\n/// into independently closable phases.\nconst DEFAULT_MITOSIS_TIMEOUT_TEMPLATE: &str = \"\\\n## Timeout Mitosis Analysis\n\nThis bead **timed out** after substantial productive work. Your job is to\nanalyze what was accomplished and decompose the REMAINING WORK into independently\nclosable phases.\n\n### Bead\n\n**Title:** {bead_title}\n\n**Description:**\n{bead_body}\n\n**Bead ID:** {bead_id}\n\n### Timeout Context\n\n**Elapsed Time:** {elapsed_duration} of {timeout_duration} ({elapsed_percent}% used)\n\n**Evidence of Activity:**\n{activity_evidence}\n\n**Existing Children:**\n{existing_children}\n\n### Your Task\n\n1. **Distinguish completed from remaining work:**\n   - What progress was made before the timeout?\n   - What deliverables are still incomplete?\n   - What work cannot be safely recovered from the partial execution?\n\n2. **Propose child beads for the REMAINING WORK ONLY:**\n   - Each child must be independently completable (no dependencies on timeout-prone work)\n   - Each child must be closable even if earlier phases in the original task timed out\n   - Focus on deliverables that can be completed within normal time limits\n\n3. **Refuse decomposition if appropriate:**\n   - If the bead represents a single atomic task that cannot be safely divided\n   - If the timeout was caused by infrastructure failure (not productive work)\n   - If splitting would require redoing work that may have completed partially\n   - If child tasks would require unsafe overlap with incomplete work\n\n### Output Format\n\nYou must output ONLY a JSON object (no markdown fencing, no explanation).\n\n**If the remaining work CAN be decomposed into independent phases:**\n{{\\\"splittable\\\": true, \\\"children\\\": [{{\\\"title\\\": \\\"Phase 1: remaining work\\\", \\\"body\\\": \\\"Description of what remains and acceptance criteria\\\"}}, ...]}}\n\n**If the bead is atomic (cannot be safely divided) OR the timeout was not productive:**\n{{\\\"splittable\\\": false, \\\"reason\\\": \\\"Brief explanation why decomposition is inappropriate\\\"}}\n\n### Rules for Timeout Decomposition\n\n- **Split ONLY if:** Remaining work can be completed independently without redoing completed portions\n- **Each child must:** Be completable within normal time limits (not another timeout)\n- **Each child must:** Have clear acceptance criteria that don't depend on incomplete work\n- **Valid split:** Original task had 3 phases, phase 1 completed, propose children for phases 2-3\n- **Invalid split:** Any child that would require redoing work that may have finished\n- **Invalid split:** Task is atomic (e.g., \\\"run full test suite\\\" cannot be split into \\\"run half\\\")\n\n### Examples\n\n**Valid timeout split:**\n- Original: \\\"Implement OAuth flow with tests (3 phases: design, implement, test)\\\"\n- Timeout evidence: Agent completed design and partial implementation\n- Children: \\\"Complete OAuth token implementation\\\", \\\"Add comprehensive tests\\\"\n\n**Invalid timeout split (atomic task):**\n- Original: \\\"Run full integration test suite\\\"\n- Timeout evidence: Tests were running when timeout occurred\n- Result: NOT splittable (splitting would require rerunning tests from incomplete state)\n\n**Invalid timeout split (infrastructure):**\n- Original: \\\"Deploy to production\\\"\n- Timeout evidence: No tool calls, empty output (infrastructure hang)\n- Result: NOT splittable (timeout was not productive work)\";\n\n/// Built-in weave template for gap analysis and bead Analyze the bead \\\nand propose alternative approaches that could be executed by an automated \\\nagent without the human decision.\n\nFor each alternative, provide:\n- title: concise description of the alternative approach\n- body: what would be done differently\n- tradeoffs: what is gained and what is lost compared to the original approach\n\nIf no viable alternatives exist, respond with: NO_ALTERNATIVES\";\n\n/// Built-in pulse template for health scan bead creation.\nconst DEFAULT_PULSE_TEMPLATE: &str = \"\\\n## Scan Results\n\n{scan_results}\n\n## Current Open Beads\n\n{existing_beads}\n\n## Question\n\nReview the scan results above. The resolver MUST NOT implement\n/// changes or mutate beads — it only analyzes and decides.\nconst DEFAULT_RESOLVE_TEMPLATE: &str = \"\\\n## Resolve: Analyze Pluck Outcome\n\nAnalyze the completed Pluck operation and determine what should happen next.\n**CRITICAL: This is an analysis-only role. You MUST NOT implement changes, commit code,\nor mutate beads. Your ONLY job is to decide what happens next.**\n\n### Bead Context\n\n**Title:** {bead_title}\n**Bead ID:** {bead_id}\n**Description:**\n{bead_body}\n\n### Operation Outcome\n\n**Exit Code:** {exit_code}\n**Exit Status:** {exit_status}\n**Duration:** {duration}\n**Was Interrupted:** {was_interrupted}\n\n### Agent Output\n\n**Stdout:**\n{stdout}\n\n**Stderr:**\n{stderr}\n\n### Your Task\n\nAnalyze the operation outcome and choose ONE of these decisions:\n\n1. **Complete** - Task succeeded, bead should be closed\n2. **Retry** - Temporary failure, release for immediate retry\n3. **Blocked** - External dependency, cannot proceed without human input\n4. **Split** - Task decomposes into multiple independent subtasks\n\n### Decision Criteria\n\n**Choose Complete if:**\n- Exit code 0 and work was accomplished (commits, tests passed, etc.)\n- Evidence exists that the task is done (git log shows commits, artifacts built)\n- No outstanding work remains\n\n**Choose Retry if:**\n- Transient failure (network timeout, rate limit, temporary resource unavailable)\n- Exit code non-zero but fixable with same or different approach\n- No human intervention needed\n- Work is retryable without risk\n\n**Choose Blocked if:**\n- Human decision required (API key approval, design choice, credentials)\n- External dependency unavailable (service down, third-party API issue)\n- Cannot proceed without external action\n- Agent cannot reasonably proceed autonomously\n\n**Choose Split if:**\n- Bead describes multiple independent subtasks\n- Each subtask can be completed separately and closed independently\n- Splitting would parallelize work or reduce complexity\n- Parent can become an umbrella tracking progress\n\n### Required Response Format\n\nYou MUST respond with valid JSON matching this exact structure:\n\n{{\\\n  \\\"decision\\\": {{\\\n    \\\"complete\\\": {{\\\n      \\\"evidence\\\": \\\"What proves success (commits, tests, artifacts)\\\",\\\n      \\\"summary\\\": \\\"One-line summary of what was accomplished\\\"\\\n    }}\\\n  }}\\\n}}\n\nOR\n\n{{\\\n  \\\"decision\\\": {{\\\n    \\\"retry\\\": {{\\\n      \\\"reason\\\": \\\"Why the attempt failed (error message, diagnostic)\\\",\\\n      \\\"strategy\\\": \\\"same\\\" | \\\"increase_timeout\\\" | \\\"different_approach\\\" | \\\"backoff\\\"\\\n    }}\\\n  }}\\\n}}\n\nOR\n\n{{\\\n  \\\"decision\\\": {{\\\n    \\\"blocked\\\": {{\\\n      \\\"blocker\\\": \\\"What external resource is blocking progress\\\",\\\n      \\\"required_action\\\": \\\"What action is needed from a human\\\",\\\n      \\\"severity\\\": \\\"low\\\" | \\\"medium\\\" | \\\"high\\\"\\\n    }}\\\n  }}\\\n}}\n\nOR\n\n{{\\\n  \\\"decision\\\": {{\\\n    \\\"split\\\": {{\\\n      \\\"children\\\": [\\\n        {{\\\n          \\\"title\\\": \\\"Short task title\\\",\\\n          \\\"body\\\": \\\"Task description and acceptance criteria\\\",\\\n          \\\"priority\\\": 1\\\n        }}\\\n      ],\\\n      \\\"rationale\\\": \\\"Why this decomposition is appropriate\\\"\\\n    }}\\\n  }}\\\n}}\n\n### Response Rules\n\n- Respond with ONLY valid JSON (no markdown fencing, no explanation)\n- All string fields must be non-empty\n- children array must have 1-10 items for split decisions\n- priority must be 1-4 (lower is higher priority)\n- strategy must be one of: same, increase_timeout, different_approach, backoff\n- severity must be one of: low, medium, high\n- Invalid responses will be rejected and fallback to safe retry\n\n### Prohibitions\n\n**You MUST NOT:**\n- Implement any changes to code\n- Run build commands, tests, or git operations\n- Create, modify, or delete beads\n- Commit or push anything\n- Make any side effects whatsoever\n\n**You MUST:**\n- Analyze the outcome objectively\n- Choose exactly one decision type\n- Provide complete, accurate information in decision fields\n- Respond with valid JSON only\";\n\n/// Built-in split template for auto-splitting beads with too many consecutive failures.\n///\n/// This template instructs the agent to decompose a problematic bead into\n/// smaller, focused child beads and convert the parent into an umbrella.\nconst DEFAULT_SPLIT_TEMPLATE: &str = \"\\\n## Auto-Split: Decompose This Bead\n\nThis bead has failed {failure_count} times in a row and needs to be broken down \\\ninto smaller, manageable pieces.\n\n### Bead to Split\n\n**Title:** {bead_title}\n**Bead ID:** {bead_id}\n**Description:**\n{bead_body}\n\n### Your Task\n\nYou MUST split this bead into 3-5 smaller child beads. The parent is too big \\\nor complex and has failed repeatedly. Your job is to decompose it into a \\\nchain of focused, independently achievable tasks.\n\n### Requirements\n\n1. **Create 3-5 child beads** using the active bead CLI:\n   ```bash\n   {bead_cli} create --title \\\"Child Title\\\" \\\\\n     --description \\\"Child description and acceptance criteria\\\" \\\\\n     --label split-child\n   ```\n\n2. **Each child must:**\n   - Be independently completable and closable\n   - Have a clear, focused scope\n   - Start with a verb (e.g., \\\"Add\\\", \\\"Fix\\\", \\\"Implement\\\", \\\"Write\\\")\n   - Include acceptance criteria in the body\n   - Be added with label: `split-child`\n\n3. **Chain the children sequentially:**\n   - Child 2 depends on Child 1\n   - Child 3 depends on Child 2\n   - (Continue for all children)\n\n4. **Convert this parent into an umbrella:**\n   - Add a dependency: this parent depends on the LAST child\n   - Add label: `umbrella` to this parent\n\n5. **Verify the setup:**\n   ```bash\n   {bead_cli} show {bead_id}  # Should show umbrella label and dependency on last child\n   {bead_cli} show <last-child-id>  # Should show this parent as a dependent\n   ```\n\n   Chain and label with:\n   ```bash\n   {dep_add_command}\n   {bead_cli} label add <bead-id> --label split-child\n   ```\n\n### Example\n\nIf splitting \\\"Build authentication system with OAuth and JWT\\\":\n1. Create child: \\\"Design OAuth2 flow\\\" with label split-child\n2. Create child: \\\"Implement JWT token service\\\" with label split-child, depends on child 1\n3. Create child: \\\"Add OAuth2 login endpoint\\\" with label split-child, depends on child 2\n4. Parent depends on child 3 and gets umbrella label\n\n### Output Format\n\nAfter creating all children and wiring dependencies, output:\n```\nSPLIT_COMPLETE: Created N children, parent converted to umbrella\n```\n\nList the created child IDs:\n```\nChildren: needle-xxx, needle-yyy, needle-zzz\n```\n\nDo NOT close this bead. Just verify the split is complete and output the \\\nSPLIT_COMPLETE message.\";\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Known template names and their allowed variables\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Common variables available to all templates.\nconst COMMON_VARS: &[&str] = &[\n    \"{bead_id}\",\n    \"{bead_title}\",\n    \"{bead_body}\",\n    \"{bead_comments}\",\n    \"{workspace_path}\",\n    \"{context_file_contents}\",\n    \"{workspace_instructions}\",\n    \"{worker_id}\",\n    \"{bead_cli}\",\n    \"{dep_add_command}\",\n];\n\n/// Returns the extra (strand-specific) variables allowed for a given template name.\n/// Returns `None` for unknown template names.\nfn extra_vars_for_template(name: &str) -> Option<&'static [&'static str]> {\n    match name {\n        \"pluck\" => Some(&[]),\n        \"split\" => Some(&[\"{failure_count}\"]),\n        \"mitosis\" => Some(&[\"{existing_children}\"]),\n        \"mitosis-timeout\" => Some(&[\n            \"{existing_children}\",\n            \"{elapsed_duration}\",\n            \"{timeout_duration}\",\n            \"{elapsed_percent}\",\n            \"{activity_evidence}\",\n        ]),\n        \"weave\" => Some(&[\"{doc_files}\", \"{existing_beads}\"]),\n        \"unravel\" => Some(&[\"{human_bead_context}\"]),\n        \"pulse\" => Some(&[\"{scan_results}\", \"{existing_beads}\"]),\n        \"resolve\" => Some(&[\n            \"{exit_code}\",\n            \"{duration}\",\n            \"{stdout}\",\n            \"{stderr}\",\n            \"{exit_status}\",\n            \"{was_interrupted}\",\n        ]),\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\nfn bead_commands_for_workspace(workspace: &Path) -> (&'static str, &'static str) {\n    let backend = std::fs::read_to_string(workspace.join(\".needle.yaml\"))\n        .ok()\n        .and_then(|text| serde_yaml::from_str::<serde_yaml::Value>(&text).ok())\n        .and_then(|value| {\n            value\n                .get(\"bead_cli\")?\n                .get(\"backend\")?\n                .as_str()\n                .map(str::to_string)\n        });\n    if matches!(backend.as_deref(), Some(\"bead\" | \"bead-rs\")) {\n        (\n            \"bead\",\n            \"bead dep add <blocked-id> <blocker-id> --kind blocks\",\n        )\n    } else {\n        (\"bf\", \"bf dep add <blocker-id> --blocks <blocked-id>\")\n    }\n}\n\n/// All known built-in template names (used in tests to verify defaults).\n#[cfg(test)]\nconst KNOWN_TEMPLATE_NAMES: &[&str] = &[\n    \"pluck\",\n    \"split\",\n    \"mitosis\",\n    \"mitosis-timeout\",\n    \"weave\",\n    \"unravel\",\n    \"pulse\",\n    \"resolve\",\n];\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// BuiltPrompt\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The rendered output of prompt construction.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct BuiltPrompt {\n    /// The fully rendered prompt string.\n    pub content: String,\n    /// SHA-256 hex digest of `content` (for telemetry reproducibility).\n    pub hash: String,\n    /// Rough token estimate (chars / 4).\n    pub token_estimate: u64,\n    /// Name of the template used to build this prompt (e.g., `\"pluck\"`).\n    pub template_name: String,\n    /// Version tag identifying which variant/version was used\n    /// (e.g., `\"pluck-default\"`, `\"pluck-v2\"`).\n    pub template_version: String,\n}\n\n/// Dynamic context added to a timeout-triggered mitosis prompt.\npub struct MitosisTimeoutContext<'a> {\n    pub elapsed_duration: &'a str,\n    pub timeout_duration: &'a str,\n    pub elapsed_percent: &'a str,\n    pub activity_evidence: &'a str,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// PromptBuilder\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Constructs agent prompts from bead context.\n///\n/// All five named templates (`pluck`, `mitosis`, `weave`, `unravel`, `pulse`)\n/// are always present with built-in defaults. User-provided overrides from\n/// config replace specific templates while others keep their defaults.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct PromptBuilder {\n    /// Named templates. All five built-in names are always present.\n    templates: BTreeMap<String, String>,\n    /// Paths to context files (relative to the workspace root).\n    context_file_paths: Vec<std::path::PathBuf>,\n    /// Free-form workspace instructions appended to prompts.\n    workspace_instructions: Option<String>,\n    /// Cached learnings content for the workspace (if exists).\n    learnings_content: Option<String>,\n    /// Cached global learnings content (cross-workspace patterns, if exists).\n    global_learnings_content: Option<String>,\n    /// Skill library for matching and injecting relevant skills into prompts.\n    skill_library: Option<SkillLibrary>,\n    /// A/B test variant configurations per template name.\n    variants: BTreeMap<String, Vec<VariantConfig>>,\n}\n\nimpl PromptBuilder {\n    /// Create a new `PromptBuilder` from prompt config.\n    ///\n    /// Initializes all built-in templates, then overrides any that are\n    /// specified in `config.templates`.\n    pub fn new(config: &PromptConfig) -> Self {\n        let mut templates = BTreeMap::new();\n        templates.insert(\"pluck\".to_string(), DEFAULT_PLUCK_TEMPLATE.to_string());\n        templates.insert(\"split\".to_string(), DEFAULT_SPLIT_TEMPLATE.to_string());\n        templates.insert(\"mitosis\".to_string(), DEFAULT_MITOSIS_TEMPLATE.to_string());\n        templates.insert(\n            \"mitosis-timeout\".to_string(),\n            DEFAULT_MITOSIS_TIMEOUT_TEMPLATE.to_string(),\n        );\n        templates.insert(\"weave\".to_string(), DEFAULT_WEAVE_TEMPLATE.to_string());\n        templates.insert(\"unravel\".to_string(), DEFAULT_UNRAVEL_TEMPLATE.to_string());\n        templates.insert(\"pulse\".to_string(), DEFAULT_PULSE_TEMPLATE.to_string());\n        templates.insert(\"resolve\".to_string(), DEFAULT_RESOLVE_TEMPLATE.to_string());\n\n        // Apply user overrides (partial: only specified templates are replaced).\n        for (name, body) in &config.templates {\n            templates.insert(name.clone(), body.clone());\n        }\n\n        PromptBuilder {\n            templates,\n            context_file_paths: config.context_files.clone(),\n            workspace_instructions: config.instructions.clone(),\n            learnings_content: None,\n            global_learnings_content: None,\n            skill_library: None,\n            variants: config.variants.clone(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new `PromptBuilder` with workspace-specific learnings.\n    ///\n    /// This variant loads the `.beads/learnings.md` file if it exists,\n    /// automatically injecting workspace learnings into all prompts.\n    pub fn with_workspace(config: &PromptConfig, workspace: &Path) -> Result<Self> {\n        let mut builder = Self::new(config);\n\n        // Load learnings if the file exists.\n        let learnings = LearningsFile::load(workspace);\n        if let Ok(learnings_file) = learnings {\n            if !learnings_file.entries().is_empty() {\n                builder.learnings_content = Some(learnings_file.to_prompt_content());\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Load skill library (missing directory is silently ignored).\n        if let Ok(lib) = SkillLibrary::load(workspace) {\n            if !lib.is_empty() {\n                builder.skill_library = Some(lib);\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(builder)\n    }\n\n    /// Load skills from additional workspaces whose skill labels match the given\n    /// workspace labels, merging them with any locally-loaded skills.\n    ///\n    /// This implements cross-workspace skill sharing: a skill tagged `[rust, api]`\n    /// in another workspace is made available here if this workspace's labels\n    /// include `rust` or `api`. All skills (local + cross-workspace) are ranked\n    /// together by `match_score` and `success_count` at prompt-build time.\n    ///\n    /// Silently ignores workspaces with no skills directory.\n    pub fn with_cross_workspace_skills(\n        mut self,\n        workspaces: &[std::path::PathBuf],\n        workspace_labels: &[String],\n    ) -> Self {\n        if workspace_labels.is_empty() || workspaces.is_empty() {\n            return self;\n        }\n\n        let mut lib = self\n            .skill_library\n            .take()\n            .unwrap_or_else(crate::skill::SkillLibrary::new_empty);\n\n        for workspace in workspaces {\n            lib.extend_from_workspace(workspace, workspace_labels);\n        }\n\n        if !lib.is_empty() {\n            self.skill_library = Some(lib);\n        }\n\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Load global learnings from the given path into this builder.\n    ///\n    /// Global learnings are cross-workspace patterns promoted by the consolidator.\n    /// They are injected after workspace learnings, before skills.\n    /// Missing or empty files are silently ignored.\n    pub fn with_global_learnings(mut self, path: &Path) -> Self {\n        if let Ok(file) = GlobalLearningsFile::load(path) {\n            let content = file.to_prompt_content();\n            if !content.is_empty() {\n                self.global_learnings_content = Some(content);\n            }\n        }\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// Validate all templates at boot time.\n    ///\n    /// For each known template, checks that every `{variable}` reference in the\n    /// template body is a recognized variable. Returns an error listing all\n    /// invalid references found.\n    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let mut errors = Vec::new();\n\n        for (name, body) in &self.templates {\n            let allowed_extra = extra_vars_for_template(name);\n\n            // Extract all {variable} references from the template body.\n            // Skip escaped braces ({{ and }}) used for literal JSON.\n            let vars = extract_template_vars(body);\n\n            for var in vars {\n                let is_common = COMMON_VARS.contains(&var.as_str());\n                let is_extra = allowed_extra\n                    .map(|extras| extras.contains(&var.as_str()))\n                    .unwrap_or(false);\n\n                if !is_common && !is_extra {\n                    errors.push(format!(\"template \\\"{name}\\\": unknown variable {var}\"));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        if errors.is_empty() {\n            Ok(())\n        } else {\n            bail!(\"invalid prompt template(s):\\n  {}\", errors.join(\"\\n  \"));\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Build the prompt for a claimed bead using the named template.\n    ///\n    /// Common variables (`{bead_id}`, `{bead_title}`, etc.) are always substituted.\n    /// Missing context files are silently omitted.\n    pub fn build(\n        &self,\n        bead: &Bead,\n        workspace: &Path,\n        worker_id: &str,\n        template_name: &str,\n    ) -> Result<BuiltPrompt> {\n        self.build_with_vars(bead, workspace, worker_id, template_name, &[])\n    }\n\n    /// Build the prompt with additional strand-specific variables.\n    ///\n    /// `extra_vars` is a slice of `(variable_name, value)` pairs for\n    /// strand-specific substitutions (e.g., `(\"{doc_files}\", \"...\")` for weave).\n    #[tracing::instrument(\n        name = \"bead.prompt_build\",\n        skip(self, bead, workspace, extra_vars),\n        fields(\n            needle.bead.id = %bead.id,\n            needle.prompt.template_name = %template_name,\n            needle.prompt.template_version = tracing::field::Empty,\n            needle.prompt.token_estimate = tracing::field::Empty,\n        )\n    )]\n    pub fn build_with_vars(\n        &self,\n        bead: &Bead,\n        workspace: &Path,\n        worker_id: &str,\n        template_name: &str,\n        extra_vars: &[(&str, &str)],\n    ) -> Result<BuiltPrompt> {\n        // Resolve template: variant takes precedence over built-in.\n        let (template_version, variant_content) =\n            self.select_variant(worker_id, template_name, workspace);\n        let template_content: &str = match variant_content {\n            Some(ref c) => c.as_str(),\n            None => self\n                .templates\n                .get(template_name)\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"unknown prompt template: {template_name}\"))?\n                .as_str(),\n        };\n\n        // Build context section: files + learnings + matching skills (in that order).\n        let mut context_parts = vec![self.load_context_files(workspace)];\n        if let Some(ref lib) = self.skill_library {\n            let matching = lib.matching_skills(&bead.labels, &bead.title);\n            if !matching.is_empty() {\n                let skill_content = SkillLibrary::to_prompt_content(&matching);\n                context_parts.push(skill_content);\n            }\n        }\n        let context_file_contents = context_parts\n            .into_iter()\n            .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join(\"\\n\\n\");\n\n        let instructions = self\n            .workspace_instructions\n            .as_deref()\n            .unwrap_or(\"(no workspace instructions)\");\n        let body = bead.body.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"(no description)\");\n\n        // Build comments section with truncation (max 2000 bytes, newest last).\n        let comments_section = format_comments(&bead.comments);\n\n        // Substitute common variables.\n        let (bead_cli, dep_add_command) = bead_commands_for_workspace(workspace);\n        let mut content = template_content\n            .replace(\"{bead_id}\", bead.id.as_ref())\n            .replace(\"{bead_title}\", &bead.title)\n            .replace(\"{bead_body}\", body)\n            .replace(\"{bead_comments}\", &comments_section)\n            .replace(\"{workspace_path}\", &workspace.display().to_string())\n            .replace(\"{context_file_contents}\", &context_file_contents)\n            .replace(\"{workspace_instructions}\", instructions)\n            .replace(\"{worker_id}\", worker_id)\n            .replace(\"{bead_cli}\", bead_cli)\n            .replace(\"{dep_add_command}\", dep_add_command);\n\n        // Substitute strand-specific variables.\n        for (var, value) in extra_vars {\n            content = content.replace(var, value);\n        }\n\n        let hash = hex_sha256(&content);\n        let token_estimate = content.len() as u64 / 4;\n\n        // Record span attributes\n        tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.prompt.template_version\", &template_version);\n        tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.prompt.token_estimate\", token_estimate);\n\n        Ok(BuiltPrompt {\n            content,\n            hash,\n            token_estimate,\n            template_name: template_name.to_string(),\n            template_version,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Convenience method that uses the `\"pluck\"` template.\n    pub fn build_pluck(\n        &self,\n        bead: &Bead,\n        workspace: &Path,\n        worker_id: &str,\n    ) -> Result<BuiltPrompt> {\n        self.build(bead, workspace, worker_id, \"pluck\")\n    }\n\n    /// Build a split (auto-split) prompt.\n    ///\n    /// `failure_count` — the current consecutive failure count for the bead.\n    pub fn build_split(\n        &self,\n        bead: &Bead,\n        workspace: &Path,\n        worker_id: &str,\n        failure_count: u32,\n    ) -> &failure_count.to_string())],\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Build a weave (gap analysis) prompt.\n    ///\n    /// `doc_files` — formatted listing of documentation files and contents.\n    /// &str,\n        existing_beads: &str,\n    ) -> Result<BuiltPrompt> {\n        self.build_with_vars(\n            bead,\n            workspace,\n            worker_id,\n            \"weave\",\n            &[\n                (\"{doc_files}\", doc_files),\n                (\"{existing_beads}\", existing_beads),\n            ],\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Build an unravel (alternative proposals)   worker_id: &str,\n        human_bead_context: &str,\n    ) -> Result<BuiltPrompt> {\n        self.build_with_vars(\n            bead,\n            workspace,\n            worker_id,\n #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\n    pub fn build_resolve(\n        &self,\n        bead: &Bead,\n        workspace: &Path,\n        worker_id: &str,\n        exit_code: i32,\n        duration: &str,\n        stdout: &str,\n        stderr: &str,\n        exit_status: &str,\n        was_interrupted: &str,\n    ) -> Result<BuiltPrompt> {\n        self.build_with_vars(\n            bead,\n     (\"{stdout}\", stdout),\n                (\"{stderr}\", stderr),\n                (\"{exit_status}\", exit_status),\n                (\"{was_interrupted}\", was_interrupted),\n            ],\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Returns an iterator over all template names.\n    pub fn template_names(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {\n        self.templates.keys().map(|s| s.as_str())\n    }\n\n    /// Load and concatenate context files from the workspace.\n    ///\n    /// Each file is prefixed with a header showing the file path.\n    /// Missing files are silently skipped.\n    fn load_context_files(&self, workspace: &Path) -> String {\n        let mut sections = Vec::new();\n\n        // Load configured context files\n        for rel_path in &self.context_file_paths {\n            let abs_path = workspace.join(rel_path);\n            match std::fs::read_to_string(&abs_path) {\n                Ok(contents) => {\n                    sections.push(format!(\n                        \"### {}\\n\\n{}\",\n                        rel_path.display(),\n                        contents.trim_end()\n                    ));\n                }\n                Err(_) => {\n                    // Silently omit missing files per spec.\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Append workspace learnings if available\n        if let Some(ref learnings) = self.learnings_content {\n            sections.push(learnings.clone());\n        }\n\n        // Append global learnings after workspace learnings (cross-workspace patterns)\n        if let Some(ref global) = self.global_learnings_content {\n            sections.push(global.clone());\n        }\n\n        if sections.is_empty() {\n            \"(no context files found)\".to_string()\n        } else {\n            sections.join(\"\\n\\n\")\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Select the variant version for a given template and worker.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `(template_version, variant_content)`:\n    /// - `template_version`: e.g. `\"pluck-default\"` or `\"pluck-v2\"`\n    /// - `variant_content`: `Some(String)` if a variant file was loaded, `None` for the default\n    ///\n    /// Assignment is deterministic: `worker_bucket(worker_id)` in `[0, 99]` is compared\n    /// against cumulative variant weights.  Same `worker_id` always produces the same result.\n    fn select_variant(\n        &self,\n        worker_id: &str,\n        template_name: &str,\n        workspace: &Path,\n    ) -> (String, Option<String>) {\n        let Some(variants) = self.variants.get(template_name) else {\n            return (format!(\"{template_name}-default\"), None);\n        };\n\n        if variants.is_empty() {\n            return (format!(\"{template_name}-default\"), None);\n        }\n\n        let bucket = worker_bucket(worker_id);\n        let mut cumulative: u32 = 0;\n\n        for variant in variants {\n            cumulative += u32::from(variant.weight);\n            if u32::from(bucket) < cumulative {\n                let abs_path = workspace.join(&variant.content_file);\n                match std::fs::read_to_string(&abs_path) {\n                    Ok(content) => {\n                        return (format!(\"{template_name}-{}\", variant.name), Some(content));\n                    }\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        // Content file missing — fall back to the built-in default.\n                        return (format!(\"{template_name}-default\"), None);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Cumulative weights < 100: worker falls outside all variant ranges.\n        (format!(\"{template_name}-default\"), None)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Helpers\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Compute the worker's variant bucket: `hash(worker_id) % 100` in `[0, 99]`.\n///\n/// Uses the first 8 bytes of the SHA-256 digest of `worker_id` as a `u64`,\n/// then takes modulo 100.  The result is deterministic and stable.\nfn worker_bucket(worker_id: &str) -> u8 {\n    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();\n    hasher.update(worker_id.as_bytes());\n    let result = hasher.finalize();\n    let n = u64::from_le_bytes(result[..8].try_into().expect(\"sha256 is at least 8 bytes\"));\n    (n % 100) as u8\n}\n\n/// Compute the SHA-256 hex digest of a string.\nfn hex_sha256(s: &str) -> String {\n    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();\n    hasher.update(s.as_bytes());\n    let result = hasher.finalize();\n    // Format as lowercase hex\n    result.iter().fold(String::with_capacity(64), |mut acc, b| {\n        use std::fmt::Write;\n        let _ = write!(acc, \"{b:02x}\");\n        acc\n    })\n}\n\n/// Format bead comments for inclusion in the prompt.\n///\n/// Comments are rendered with newest first (reverse chronological order).\n/// Total output is capped at `MAX_COMMENTS_BYTES`; if exceeded, the oldest\n/// comments are truncated and a note is appended.\n///\n/// The format includes:\n/// - Author and timestamp for each comment\n/// - Clear delimiters between comments\n/// - Explicit instruction that later comments supersede earlier ones\nfn format_comments(comments: &[crate::types::Comment]) -> String {\n    const MAX_COMMENTS_BYTES: usize = 2000;\n\n    if comments.is_empty() {\n        return String::new();\n    }\n\n    let mut output = String::from(\"## Comments (newest first)\\n\\n\");\n    output.push_str(\n        \"IMPORTANT: Later comments supersede the description above. \\\n        If a comment conflicts with the description, follow the comment.\\n\\n\",\n    );\n\n    // Sort comments by created_at descending (newest first) and accumulate\n    let mut sorted_comments: Vec<_> = comments.iter().collect();\n    sorted_comments.sort_by_key(|comment| std::cmp::Reverse(comment.created_at));\n\n    let mut total_bytes = output.len();\n    let mut truncated = false;\n    let mut displayed_count = 0;\n\n    for (idx, comment) in sorted_comments.iter().enumerate() {\n        let comment_text = format!(\n            \"### Comment {} (by {}, {})\\n{}\\n\\n\",\n            idx + 1,\n            comment.author,\n            comment.created_at.format(\"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S UTC\"),\n            comment.text\n        );\n\n        // Check if adding this comment would exceed the cap\n        if total_bytes + comment_text.len() > MAX_COMMENTS_BYTES {\n            truncated = true;\n            break;\n        }\n\n        output.push_str(&comment_text);\n        total_bytes += comment_text.len();\n        displayed_count += 1;\n    }\n\n    if truncated {\n        let omitted = sorted_comments.len() - displayed_count;\n        let note = format!(\n            \"[{} older comment(s) omitted due to length cap - showing only newest comments above]\\n\\n\",\n            omitted\n        );\n        output.push_str(&note);\n    }\n\n    output\n}\n\n/// Extract all `{variable}` references from a template string.\n///\n/// Skips escaped braces (`{{` and `}}`) which are used for literal JSON.\n/// Returns unique variable references including the braces (e.g., `\"{bead_id}\"`).\nfn extract_template_vars(template: &str) -> Vec<String> {\n    let mut vars = Vec::new();\n    let chars: Vec<char> = template.chars().collect();\n    let len = chars.len();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < len {\n        if chars[i] == '{' {\n            // Skip escaped braces: {{\n            if i + 1 < len && chars[i + 1] == '{' {\n                i += 2;\n                continue;\n            }\n            // Find matching closing brace.\n            if let Some(end) = chars[i + 1..].iter().position(|&c| c == '}') {\n                let end = i + 1 + end;\n                let var_name: String = chars[i..=end].iter().collect();\n                // Only include if it looks like a valid variable (alphanumeric + underscore).\n                let inner: String = chars[i + 1..end].iter().collect();\n                if !inner.is_empty()\n                    && inner.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_')\n                    && !vars.contains(&var_name)\n                {\n                    vars.push(var_name);\n                }\n                i = end + 1;\n            } else {\n                i += 1;\n            }\n        } else {\n            i += 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    vars\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n//
